phase: Phase 3: File playback in the AudioBus
summary: T6i blocks ordinary inherited event names, but it does not guard the in-flight current-map check. A remap to an inherited-only event can still install and play the old file.
blocking_findings: F1 [Blocker] review-a: src/apk3d/audio/bus.ts:122,278; T6i adds an own-property guard to requestFile, but the in-flight validation still reads this.files.events[name] without checking ownership. Reproduction: start a load for an own event tap->tap, then call useSoundFiles with the same base and an events object inheriting tap->tap but with no own tap property. useSoundFiles compares inherited values as equal and does not invalidate the load; isCurrent also accepts the inherited value, installs the old decoded buffer, and play('tap') can play a file for an unmapped event. This contradicts the own-property guard's unmapped-event behavior. Check ownership in all event-map reads and add a regression test for an in-flight load followed by an inherited-only remap.
evidence: T6i changes src/apk3d/audio/chibi.ts:24 and src/apk3d/audio/bus.ts:263-264. chibiPreload filters own CHIBI_EVENTS keys, and requestFile rejects non-own keys before reading their entry.

src/apk3d/audio/bus.ts:121-125 compares previous.events[name] and files.events[name] using names collected from Object.keys; a same-valued inherited property can make a formerly-own mapping appear unchanged.
src/apk3d/audio/bus.ts:275-280 isCurrent reads this.files.events[name] without Object.hasOwn, so an in-flight load can treat an inherited value as a current mapping.

tests/apk3d/audio-files.adversarial-r2.test.ts:341-363 checks inherited constructor/toString names against an ordinary Chibi map, but does not test an in-flight load followed by an inherited-only map.
